messages:
Ravi B.: Hey team, opened a small PR to harmonize wording for 'route' vs 'endpoint' across quickstart and migration guides. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4999
Carmen H.: Thanks Ravi. Do we have a decision doc for which term to prefer? I see both used in console and API reference.
Ravi B.: Not yet. Proposal in PR: use 'endpoint' when referring to a network target (URL, API surface) and 'route' for internal routing concepts (console routes, routing policy). Short rationale in the PR description.
Owen L.: I like that split. Also, in many code snippets people used `route` as a param name. Can we standardize param names to `endpoint` in snippets for clarity?
Ravi B.: For SDK snippets, plan is to keep idiomatic names: JS/TS `endpointUrl` or `endpoint`, Python `endpoint_url` or `endpoint`. Changed a couple of offending examples.
Carmen H.: Small nit: adjust any sentence that previously said "call the route" to "call the endpoint" where it means making a network request. Otherwise fine.
Ravi B.: Good catch. Did a find/replace for the docs dir and left comments on ambiguous hits.
docs-bot: PR #4999 opened by @Ravi B. - checklist: docs review, snippet scan, console-label cross-check.
Owen L.: I'll run the snippet extractor against the registry and post diffs. If any snippet ids break, I'll create redirects in the registry.
Carmen H.: Please also add one-line entry in STYLE.md explaining the endpoint/route distinction so future authors follow it.
Ravi B.: Added a single paragraph to STYLE.md in the PR and linked it from the migration guide.
Owen L.: Ran extractor: two JS snippets used `route` as a variable name. Pushed trivial fixes. All tests green locally.
Carmen H.: Great. I'll give the PR a quick pass and merge after docs-bot link-check completes. :thumbsup:
Ravi B.: Thanks everyone. If any product console label conflicts come up, we'll open a follow-up with UX.
